note: The review board for the 2026-11-16 request. It exists so a reviewer can compare every possible path, see what each one costs, see what it waits on, and choose one - before any change is made. Nothing in this file is implemented: every proposal starts at AWAITING_DECISION and tools/validate_review_board.py fails the build if a row reads as done while no decision is recorded. Measured rows (PM-) come from inspecting this repository on 2026-11-16 and name the file and page they were counted from. Requirement rows (RP-) trace the 2026-11-16 brief sentence by sentence. Question rows (PQ-) exist to surface missing information; an open question carries no answer, only what is known, what is missing, and how to obtain it.
disclosure: As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.

decision_vocabulary.AWAITING_DECISION: Nobody has chosen. The row is a proposal and nothing has been built from it.
decision_vocabulary.SELECTED: The owner picked one option. Implementation is still a separate, later step and is not implied.
decision_vocabulary.DEFERRED: The owner chose not to decide yet. The row records why, and what would make it decidable.

requirements.brief_clause: Build an AI-powered Amazon affiliate marketing platform that automates product research
requirements.asks_for: A research capability that finds and evaluates products without a human doing the search.
requirements.what_exists: A scoring module, an ASIN guard, a link builder and a tracking schema exist as code in tools/ (scoring.py, asin_guard.py, link_builder.py, tracking_schema.sql). What does not exist is a record of the module having chosen, ranked or rejected any real product.
requirements.what_is_missing: A dated run of the research module against a real candidate set, with its output stored. Without that, 'AI-powered research' is a claim about code, not about results.
requirements.verified_against: no official page defines what 'automates product research' must produce - file inspection only

requirements.brief_clause: identifies trending and high-converting products, analyzes pricing, reviews, competition, and commission potential
requirements.asks_for: Five measured signals per product: trend, conversion, price, review volume, competition, plus commission rate.
requirements.what_exists: Nothing. No trend series, no conversion data, no stored price, no review count, no competitor set is published anywhere in this repository.
requirements.what_is_missing: Every one of the five signals, for every product. Amazon does not expose price, rating or review count to an automated fetch; the per-category commission schedule is behind sign-in (recorded as the open irregularity on the Flagged page).
requirements.verified_against: repository-wide search on 2026-11-16 for stored price, rating and review-count values returned none outside the policy statements

requirements.brief_clause: generates SEO-optimized product articles, comparisons, and buying guides
requirements.asks_for: Three page types - single-product article, comparison, buying guide - written to rank.
requirements.what_exists: All three page types exist and are published: 3 product articles (marketing/articles/p1..p3), a comparison (marketing/comparison.html) and a buying guide (marketing/buying-guide.html), plus 8 question-shaped guides.
requirements.what_is_missing: Ranking is not something a repository can demonstrate; only Search Console can. That measurement is PQ-04 and it is the only honest way to call this 'optimized' rather than 'optimized for'.
requirements.verified_against: tools/build_sitemap.py published_pages() on 2026-11-16: all three types present and linked

requirements.asks_for: Links that carry the owner's Associates ID and can be managed.
requirements.what_exists: A policy-checking link builder that refuses a malformed tag (tools/link_builder.py) and a preview-link mode that emits clearly labelled, non-monetised links.
requirements.what_is_missing: An Associates tag. Every product link on the site is a preview link and the site says so. As supplied, the three short links carry no tag parameter, so as supplied they cannot earn commission.

requirements.asks_for: A measurement path from click to conversion.
requirements.what_exists: Five event definitions and a SQL schema, with zero events live. The site is static and ships no analytics.
requirements.what_is_missing: A collector, a consent posture, and a decision about which events are worth collecting. All three are undecided, so nothing is collected.
requirements.verified_against: discovery/measurement.html: 5 defined events, 0 live, stated on the page

requirements.brief_clause: continuously optimize campaigns to maximize affiliate revenue
requirements.asks_for: A loop that changes the site in response to measured results.
requirements.what_exists: Nothing to optimise against: no revenue, no click data, no conversion data, and no tagged link.
requirements.what_is_missing: A first measured number. Any 'optimisation' before RP-04 and RP-05 exist would be optimisation of a guess.
requirements.verified_against: no official page can define an optimisation target for a site with no measured revenue - confirmed by reading discovery/measurement.html on 2026-11-16

requirements.asks_for: The system does the work repeatedly, without a person, and decides from data.
requirements.what_exists: Automation of the verification and publishing machinery is real and extensive: 20-plus generators, 35 replayable CI steps, and a negative test proving each gate can fail.
requirements.what_is_missing: Automation of the *commercial* work - research, selection, optimisation. The automation built so far is accuracy automation, which is not what this clause asks for.
requirements.verified_against: no official page defines 'scalable' as a measurement - counted instead from the workflow and tools/ on 2026-11-16

requirements.brief_clause: compliance with Amazon Associates policies and disclosure requirements
requirements.asks_for: Every policy obligation met, with evidence.
requirements.what_exists: The strongest part of the build: a control ledger of 20 rules mapped to implemented controls, the mandated sentence on every published page, rel=sponsored on outbound product links, a link builder that refuses non-compliant tags, and a build that fails if a page is missing the disclosure.
requirements.what_is_missing: Three items that no amount of code can close: an approved account, a tagged link, and a site the owner owns on a domain the owner controls.
requirements.verified_against: tools/audit_site.py check_disclosure across 139 published pages on 2026-11-16

requirements.brief_clause: The goal of this project is to collect, organize, and analyze utilizing a full list of requirements.
requirements.asks_for: One complete requirements list, collected and analysed.
requirements.what_exists: Two requirement registers already exist and both are machine-gated: ledger/requirements.json (programme and compliance, with a closed four-value status vocabulary) and ledger/readiness.json (Amazon's Application Review Process, row by row). This register is the third and the only one that traces the 2026-11-16 brief sentence by sentence.
requirements.what_is_missing: A single joined view. The three registers currently have three different status vocabularies and no page reads all three at once; that is PS-03.
requirements.verified_against: no official page defines what a complete requirements list must contain - counted by reading the three registers on 2026-11-16

requirements.brief_clause: It should look like a polished marketing affiliate website ... It should not read like some AI slop website
requirements.asks_for: A reader-facing surface that a shopper would trust, not a build artefact.
requirements.what_exists: Good prose and a strict anti-slop rule set, enforced by a gate: a banned-phrase list, a no-superlative rule, sourced sentences, no price, no star rating, and a stated opinion in a labelled box.
requirements.what_is_missing: The page anatomy a shopper uses to buy. Measured on 2026-11-16: the 20 marketing pages carry 0 product images, the 71 product links carry citation labels rather than buy labels, the hero's primary button leads to a page with no product link, and the site's front page is an operator dashboard. That is PD-01 to PD-08.
requirements.verified_against: counted on 2026-11-16 across marketing/*.html (see the PM- rows)

requirements.brief_clause: Create a section dedicated for suggestions so someone can review suggestions and choose the best path before implementing any changes.
requirements.asks_for: A review section where the options are compared and chosen before anything is built.
requirements.what_exists: Five suggestion surfaces already existed before this task (pages/suggestions.html with SG-01..SG-12, console/, audit/, discovery/, marketing/improvements.html), plus decisions/review.html added by this task, which is the first one that scores every proposal on one scale and tracks a recorded decision.
requirements.what_is_missing: An actual owner decision. Every proposal on every board is still AWAITING_DECISION, and the boards are separate registers rather than one.
requirements.verified_against: no official page defines what a review board must look like - the six surfaces were counted on 2026-11-16; five pre-date this task

requirements.brief_clause: I want a clear list of questions, informations and answers that need to be addressed before any decision can be reasonably made
requirements.asks_for: Questions with their answers, and an explicit statement of what is unknown.
requirements.what_exists: 28 open questions across the existing registers (Q-01..Q-18 in the ledger, MQ-01..MQ-10 in the marketing set), each with what is known, what is missing and how to obtain it. Not one of them carries an answer, because the information to answer them is not in this repository.
requirements.what_is_missing: The owner's answers, and 9 further questions (PQ-01..PQ-09) that only became visible once the brief was traced sentence by sentence.

requirements.brief_clause: Suggestions need to be made to discover missing information.
requirements.asks_for: Proposals whose purpose is to surface what is not known.
requirements.what_exists: PS-03 and PS-11 are exactly this: a discovery sprint that produces the missing numbers, and a habit of pricing every proposal by the question it waits on. Every PQ- row names a named, owned action rather than an aspiration.
requirements.what_is_missing: Nothing structural in this register. The measurement that would prove it working is a first answered question, and none has been answered yet.
requirements.verified_against: this register: 12 PQ- rows each carry a non-empty obtain field naming who acts

requirements.brief_clause: Create an executive summary outlining important details.
requirements.asks_for: One page a decision-maker can read in five minutes.
requirements.what_exists: Three already: EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md at the repository root, summary.html as a published page, and zone2/docs/EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md. All three predate this task.
requirements.what_is_missing: Nothing structural. The new decision surfaces are advertised from the root page footer so a reader of the summary can reach them.
requirements.verified_against: no official page defines the contents of an executive summary - the three files were confirmed on disk and in the sitemap on 2026-11-16

requirements.brief_clause: Create a github page live site ... with a clean landing page and subpages organized by category ... simple dashboard ... table format
requirements.asks_for: A live GitHub Pages site, a clean landing page, category subpages, and a dashboard-like table view.
requirements.what_exists: 139 pages are live at kanlerxz87-cyber.github.io/Zone2, deployed by Actions on every push to main, with a table-based research hub and a decision namespace organised by category.
requirements.what_is_missing: The landing page at the site root is an operator dashboard rather than a shopper's front door; that is a design choice, and it is PD-06.
requirements.verified_against: no official page governs the arrangement of a GitHub Pages site - deployment confirmed through the GitHub Actions API on 2026-11-16

requirements.brief_clause: Every table row must have a source link to an official site. If a value can't be confirmed from an official source, leave it blank and flag it as unverified. Never infer or fill in values.
requirements.asks_for: Per-row provenance and blanks rather than guesses.
requirements.what_exists: The repository's central invariant, and it is enforced rather than asserted: gates in at least six namespaces fail a row that has neither a resolvable official source nor an explicit unverified marker, and negative tests prove each gate can fail.
requirements.what_is_missing: Nothing known. This is the practice this register reuses for itself.
requirements.verified_against: no official page states this rule - it is the project's own contract, checked instead by the six validators named in what_exists

proposals.title: Give the site a shopper-facing front door and move the operator console behind it
proposals.problem: The repository root is, by measurement, an operator dashboard: 76 navigation links in two groups, a KPI band, requirement counts and a compliance ledger. It should be the front door, and Amazon's IP License requires the site's principal purpose to be marketing Amazon products and driving sales (S80). A front page that leads with the project's own bookkeeping satisfies neither the reader nor the clause.

options.label: Keep the dashboard at the root and put a shopper entry point above the fold
options.commitment: One root edit, no moves, no redirects. The dashboard stays at the same URL and gains a single hero band that leads to the buying content.
options.cost: About one session. No URL changes, so nothing that already links here breaks.
options.risk: The root still reads as a console the moment a reader scrolls; the fix is cosmetic at the page level.

options.label: Move the operator dashboard to /console/ and make the root a publication front page
options.commitment: A real URL move, permanent redirects from the old paths, the sitemap regenerated, and every one of the 76 internal links re-pointed and re-checked.
options.cost: Two or three sessions, dominated by link repair and by the audit that must prove zero new broken links.
options.risk: Highest blast radius of any option on this board. The repository has 139 pages and a sitemap gate; a partial move fails the build.

options.label: Publish the reader front page at a subpath and advertise it from the root
options.commitment: No move at all: marketing/index.html already is a publication front page, so this is a launcher band on the root plus a clearer label in the navigation.
options.cost: Under one session. Fully reversible.
options.risk: A crawler still lands on the dashboard first, so the principal-purpose reading in S80 is unchanged.

proposals.recommendation: C as the reversible first step, then A once a tagged link exists, then B only if search performance shows the root is what a crawler judges.

proposals.title: Make the site's subject the products, and its method a feature rather than the subject
proposals.problem: The pages are exceptionally well sourced, and almost all of them talk about their own sourcing. Reading marketing/index.html end to end, the recurring subject is the discipline of the page rather than the air fryer. Google's helpful-content guidance rewards effort and originality but asks whether the content is about the thing the reader came for; the same guidance says automation should be disclosed, not that the disclosure should be the content. A shopper searching 'air fryer for a family of four' wants the answer first and the method on a linked page.

options.label: Lead every page with the answer, and move the methodology to one page it links to
options.commitment: An editorial rewrite of 9 page openers. No fact changes: every number and citation stays, and the voice gate keeps failing banned phrases, superlatives and unsourced claims.
options.cost: One focused session for the openers; the remainder of each page can stay as it is.
options.risk: Low, and it is the only option that changes what a reader sees first.

options.label: Keep the method-first voice and treat transparency as the differentiator
options.commitment: No rewrite. Accept that the audience is a reader who wants the audit trail.
options.cost: Zero.
options.risk: It is a defensible position for a specialist publication and a poor one for a site whose purpose is to send buyers to Amazon. It also leaves PM-03 to PM-08 untouched.

options.label: Split the site: a shopper publication and a separate evidence publication
options.commitment: Two audiences, two navigation trees, one shared data layer.
options.cost: Largest content change on this board; every page has to be assigned to one side.
options.risk: Doubles the surface that must each carry a disclosure and each be kept fresh within 60 days.

proposals.recommendation: A. It is the change the complaint names, it is reversible, and it changes no fact.

proposals.title: Run one discovery sprint against the five signals the brief asks for, and publish the result even if the result is 'not obtainable'
proposals.problem: Three registers already ask questions; none of them produces the numbers the brief's own second clause depends on. Price, review volume, competition and commission rate are all absent, and RP-02 is the only requirement row that is entirely NOT_MET. Asking better questions has not worked for several waves because the answers live outside the repository.

options.label: A dated, one-session research pass per product with every value either sourced or recorded as unobtainable
options.commitment: Three products, one page of output, one source per value, and an explicit 'not obtainable by automated fetch' where that is the truth.
options.cost: One session. Produces a datable artefact rather than a plan.
options.risk: Some of the five signals may come back unobtainable, which makes the brief's clause unmet in public - the correct outcome, and the opposite of what a marketing page wants to say.

options.label: Wait for an approved Associates account, then use the API
options.commitment: Depends on PQ-01 and PQ-02 closing first.
options.cost: Unknown, and outside this project's control.
options.risk: Blocks every commercial requirement behind an approval that has not happened.

options.label: Use a third-party keyword or trend tool instead of Amazon data
options.commitment: A subscription, a vendor, and a licence to cite their numbers.
options.cost: A recurring fee, and a dataset we do not own.
options.risk: Third-party numbers would sit beside official ones with no shared provenance, which is the exact failure mode this repository was built to prevent.

proposals.recommendation: A now, and B the day the account is approved. C only if A returns unobtainable for most of the five.

proposals.title: Publish the shortlist page a shopper actually searches for
proposals.problem: No page on the site contains a ranked shortlist. The buying guide explicitly declines to name a winner, on the sound principle that the specs do not separate the three models. But 'which one to buy' is the query, and Google's review guidance asks that ranked lists stand on their own. Declining to rank is a defensible editorial position and a poor commercial one, and the brief's whole purpose is to make the sale.

options.label: Publish a shortlist scoped to use cases, with the ranking rule stated inline
options.commitment: One page, three or four 'best for X' rows, each decided by a named spec and linked to its source. No score invented, no star rating.
options.cost: One session. It is the highest-intent page the site could add.
options.risk: A ranking invites disagreement. Mitigated by making the rule arithmetic and visible, and by giving one row to each use case rather than a single overall winner.

options.label: Decline to rank, and say why on the buying guide
options.commitment: No new page. Keep the current position.
options.cost: Zero.
options.risk: Leaves the query unanswered and the traffic to somebody else's ranking.

options.label: Rank only after first-hand testing exists
options.commitment: Wait for PQ-11.
options.cost: Unknown.
options.risk: Indefinite, and it conflates two different things: a spec-derived recommendation and a tested review. The FTC constraint in S87 forbids claiming experience, not ranking on published specs.

proposals.recommendation: A, with the ranking rule printed above the table and the no-experience disclosure kept.

proposals.title: Turn the citation-styled product links into buy links, keeping the source one click away
proposals.problem: Measured in PM-04: 71 of the 80 product links on the marketing pages render as a source chip such as 'M4 · www.amazon.com Amazon listing'. The link that earns the commission is styled as a footnote, and the one place a reader is asked to act says 'Amazon listing'. The source must stay - that is the project's rule - but it does not have to be the button.

options.label: A two-element pattern: a button that says what happens next, and a source chip beside it
options.commitment: One renderer change in tools/build_marketing.py, applied to all 71 links, with the source id preserved verbatim next to the button.
options.cost: One session, and it touches a generated namespace - so the generator changes and the pages are regenerated, never hand-edited.
options.risk: Low. The gate that forbids a price and requires a source on each row keeps working, and the disclosure stays in the footer and moves to the button.

options.label: Keep citation labels and add a separate 'check price at Amazon' line
options.commitment: Additive only.
options.cost: Half a session.
options.risk: Two competing treatments of the same link on one page.

options.label: Leave the links as they are until a tagged link exists
options.commitment: Nothing.
options.cost: Zero.
options.risk: Keeps the strongest anti-conversion element on the site in place for as long as the account is unapproved, which may be indefinitely.

proposals.recommendation: A. The preview-link mode already labels itself as unmonetised, so the button can be honest today and become earnable the day a tag exists.

proposals.title: Stop printing a verification date on every marketing page
proposals.problem: Every marketing page prints a date of 2026-11-14 or 2026-11-15. Amazon's review guidance asks that site content generally be within the last 60 days. A page that announces its own age fails that test every day after it is published, and it will do so while being perfectly accurate. The date was added as evidence of care and now functions as evidence of staleness.

options.label: Keep the source but drop the date from the reader-facing sentence, and publish the verification date on one page
options.commitment: An editing pass over the printed dates, with the per-row source links untouched and the dates preserved on the verification page.
options.cost: Half a session.
options.risk: Loses a visible trust signal on the article pages. Mitigated because the source links stay beside every number.

options.label: Keep the dates and set a re-verification interval that actually gets run
options.commitment: A scheduled re-fetch, with the date moved forward only when a page has genuinely been re-read.
options.cost: Recurring, and it needs a person to run it.
options.risk: A scheduled job that silently stops makes every date wrong at once.

options.label: Leave it to the owner to decide when to re-verify
options.commitment: Nothing.
options.cost: Zero.
options.risk: The 60-day condition stays unmet by default.

proposals.recommendation: A now, and B only if a real re-verification loop is staffed.

proposals.title: Resolve the image question, and ship no product photography until it is resolved
proposals.problem: There are zero photographs on 20 marketing pages, which is why the pages read as a dossier. The design notes say the rights question is open. Amazon's IP License is specific about what Program Content may be used for and how, and the licence runs only for pages whose purpose is marketing Amazon. Stock photography would put a product the site does not own at the centre of a page selling something else.

options.label: Written confirmation from Associates support on product-image use, then official image URLs only
options.commitment: One support request, one stored answer, then images sourced only from Amazon's own asset hosts.
options.cost: One email and one session once answered.
options.risk: The answer may be narrower than hoped, and it may take weeks.

options.label: Commit to a typographic identity and stop treating images as a missing feature
options.commitment: A deliberate no-photography design: large numbers, spec diagrams drawn as HTML and CSS, and comparison tables as the visual centrepiece.
options.cost: One design session.
options.risk: That is the current position, and the measured result is what the complaint is about, so this option changes nothing unless the typography gets substantially stronger.

options.label: Use licensed stock photography of food and kitchens, never of the product
options.commitment: A licence, attribution, and a rule that no stock image implies we photographed the appliance.
options.cost: A licence fee, plus a sourcing note on every page.
options.risk: Improves warmth and adds a licensing surface that has to be maintained.

proposals.recommendation: A and B together: request the answer, and meanwhile make the typographic identity deliberate and better rather than merely absent.

proposals.title: Decide, in writing, who the site is for - because four of its features cannot both be right
proposals.problem: The site is currently both a buyer's publication and an operator's console, and the same navigation serves both. That is why the root has 76 links, why the disclosure competes with a verification banner, and why a shopper meets a word like 'plpRedirect' within one screen. Twice already the registers ask this (Q-06, MQ-01) and it has never been answered, so every later design decision inherits the ambiguity.

options.label: Shopper first; the operator views stay reachable but are labelled internal
options.commitment: A stated audience, and every page gets one label: reader or owner.
options.cost: One decision plus a labelling pass over 139 pages.
options.risk: Some owner pages become one click less convenient. That is the intended trade.

options.label: Dual purpose, with the root acting as a hub that asks which you are
options.commitment: A choice screen at the root.
options.cost: One session.
options.risk: Adds a click for everybody and satisfies the principal-purpose test least well.

options.label: Operator first, with the reader pages treated as output rather than as a destination
options.commitment: An explicit statement that this is a working research repository.
options.cost: Zero edits, one honest sentence.
options.risk: It contradicts the brief's request for a marketing website. Defensible only if that request is withdrawn.

proposals.recommendation: A. Every other proposal on this board is easier to score once this is answered.

proposals.title: Publish an authorship and method statement, and make it true
proposals.problem: No marketing page carries an author. Search guidance asks who created the content and explicitly treats fabricated profiles as deception; it also asks how automated content was produced and disclosed. This project's pages are generated by a pipeline from a fact register, which is a legitimate and unusual production method, and it is disclosed nowhere in reader-facing language.

options.label: One 'how this site is made' page, linked from every article, naming the pipeline and the editor's role
options.commitment: A real page describing the actual process, including that pages are generated from a register and reviewed by a named person if one exists.
options.cost: One session, and it is honest immediately because the process is already documented internally.
options.risk: Requires deciding whether there is a named human. If there is not, the page must say so plainly rather than leave a gap.

options.label: Add a byline with a persona
options.commitment: A fictional author.
options.cost: Zero.
options.risk: Not available. Search guidance names fabricated profiles as a form of deception, and this repository's own rule V-09 forbids an invented author.

options.label: Say nothing about authorship
options.commitment: Nothing.
options.cost: Zero.
options.risk: Leaves a trust signal absent on the pages that most need one.

proposals.recommendation: A. It is the one option that is both permitted and useful.

proposals.title: Move the link-level disclosure onto the link
proposals.problem: The mandated sentence is on every page and always in the footer or a banner. FTC guidance says the disclosure should be placed with the endorsement message itself and not only where a reader must go looking. The three product articles do carry an in-context '(paid link)' marker; the 17 other pages that carry product links do not.

options.label: Every product link gets a visible adjacent marker, generated rather than typed
options.commitment: One renderer change plus a gate that fails a product link without an adjacent marker.
options.cost: One session.
options.risk: Low, and it converts a reviewer's question into a build failure.

options.label: Keep the footer sentence and the three article markers
options.commitment: Nothing.
options.cost: Zero.
options.risk: Knowingly leaves 17 pages in a weaker position than the three that do it properly.

proposals.recommendation: A. It is a one-session change that closes a stated policy gap on 17 pages.

proposals.title: Adopt a one-screen proposal template so every future suggestion arrives decidable
proposals.problem: This board, and the six that precede it, contain proposals that cannot be compared: different registers, different scales, different vocabularies, and none of them carrying a recorded decision. The result is what the brief complains about - a reader cannot choose the best path because no two rows are on the same scale.

options.label: Mandate the template this register uses: problem, three options with cost and risk, a recommendation, the question it waits on, and four scores
options.commitment: A short rule in the contribution guide, and the validator refuses a proposal missing any field.
options.cost: Already built as part of this task.
options.risk: None material. Scores are self-assessed, so they must never be presented as measurements.

options.label: Leave each board's own format alone
options.commitment: Nothing.
options.cost: Zero.
options.risk: Seven incompatible boards keep growing.

proposals.recommendation: A, with the scores printed as an explicitly self-assessed ordering aid rather than as evidence.

proposals.title: Consolidate the seven decision boards into one index, and stop adding an eighth
proposals.problem: Measured in PM-09: six boards published proposals before this task and this task adds a seventh. Each was built in good faith by a different session, and a reader looking for 'the suggestions' has no way to know which one is authoritative. The brief asks for a section where someone can review suggestions and choose; seven sections is not one.

options.label: A single index page that lists every board, its row count, its owner and whether it carries recorded decisions
options.commitment: One page and one link from every board back to it. No board is deleted and no other session's register is edited.
options.cost: One session, and it is additive so it cannot conflict with a session that owns one of the boards.
options.risk: None to correctness; it does not reduce the number of boards, it makes the number visible.

options.label: Retire five boards and migrate their rows into one register
options.commitment: Migrating the rows of five boards into one register.
options.cost: Large, and unsafe while another session is active.
options.risk: High: the coordination rule forbids editing another session's files, and a migration would touch five.

options.label: Do nothing; each board serves a different reader
options.commitment: Nothing.
options.cost: Zero.
options.risk: The stated purpose - one place to choose a path - stays unmet.

proposals.recommendation: A first, and B only in a final integration session with no other session active. Either way this row stays awaiting your decision: nothing is consolidated until you record one.

questions.question: Is there an approved Associates account, and what is its Associate ID and marketplace?
questions.known: No Associate ID is stored anywhere in this repository, and the marketing fact base records associates_tag_configured as false. The three supplied short links carry no tag parameter (re-observed 2026-11-16). Amazon requires at least three qualifying sales within 180 days before an application is reviewed, and personal orders do not count.
questions.missing: Approval status, Associate ID, and target marketplace. All three live in the owner's associates account, which this project cannot read.
questions.obtain: The owner signs in to Associates Central and records the status, ID and marketplace. A public 'one-line' answer is the only thing any of this needs.

questions.question: Do the three supplied short links carry the owner's tracking ID, or were they minted elsewhere?
questions.known: Each resolution on 2026-11-16 carries plpRedirect=mhFallback, lv=shuf, a per-fetch btn_ref and a channelId, and no Associates tag parameter. The three tokens are 9 characters; an ASIN is 10.
questions.missing: The provenance of the links and the intended products. Two readings are still open and this register does not resolve them: the links may be untagged share links for these three listings, or they may be fallback redirects that happen to land on related items.
questions.obtain: The owner opens the links in their own browser while signed in to Associates Central and reports the destination and whether a tag is attached; or re-issues the links from the product-link tool in their own account.

questions.question: Which source is permitted to supply trend and demand data?
questions.known: No trend, demand or competition data is stored in this repository. Amazon's licence is explicit that Product Advertising Content may not be used to aggregate, analyse or repurpose it, and that automated collection of product data is constrained.
questions.missing: An authorised source, its terms, and whether this project may republish a figure derived from it.
questions.obtain: The owner selects and pays for a keyword or trend tool, or confirms that only figures the site can source to an official page may appear - in which case some of the brief's clause cannot be met at all, and the site should say so.

questions.question: Has the live site any measurable organic traffic, and from which queries?
questions.known: Nothing. The repository ships no analytics and the measurement plan states 5 defined events and 0 live. Search Console is not connected.
questions.missing: Impressions, clicks, and query terms. Without these, 'SEO-optimized' cannot be distinguished from 'written with SEO in mind'.
questions.obtain: The owner verifies the domain in Google Search Console and reports a first 28-day snapshot. This does not require a tag, an account, or a paid tool.

questions.question: Who is the named editor or author, and do they exist?
questions.known: No marketing page carries an author. The project's own voice rule V-09 forbids an invented author, and search guidance names fabricated profiles as deception.
questions.missing: A real person, or an explicit decision to publish as an unedited automated publication and say so.
questions.obtain: The owner names the responsible person or states that there is none. Either answer is publishable; silence is not.

questions.question: Will the site run on a domain the owner owns, and which exact URL will be declared in the Associates application?
questions.known: The site is at kanlerxz87-cyber.github.io and Amazon's review page states that an applicant must own the website and that a rejected application is not reassessed. Two readings of the GitHub Pages subdomain against that sentence are live in the registers and this task does not settle them.
questions.missing: Whether a custom domain is owned, and which URL will be declared.
questions.obtain: The owner either registers a domain and points it at this repository or states that the github.io address is the intended declared site. A domain registration is the only action that closes it.

questions.question: Who re-verifies the pages, how often, and what happens if nobody does?
questions.known: Every marketing page prints a 2026-11-14 or 2026-11-15 verification date. Amazon asks that content generally be within the last 60 days. No scheduled job re-fetches the sources.
questions.missing: An owner for the loop, an interval, and a fallback policy for when the loop stops.
questions.obtain: The owner names the person and the interval, or approves PS-06 option A so that a stale date cannot accrue in public.

questions.question: May the site use Amazon product imagery, and under which part of the licence?
questions.known: Zero images are published. Amazon's licence permits Program Content use on pages whose principal purpose is marketing Amazon, requires each use to link to the relevant Amazon page, and restricts use in mobile applications. No written confirmation specific to this site exists in the repository.
questions.missing: A written answer that says whether product images may appear, and on what condition.
questions.obtain: The owner sends one question to Associates support and stores the reply verbatim. That reply, not this register, becomes the source.

questions.question: Are these three products the whole programme, or the first three of a larger category?
questions.known: All three listings are air fryers. The repository already records the portfolio as single-category. Nine question-shaped guides and three product articles are built around exactly these three models.
questions.missing: Whether the intent is depth on three products or breadth across the category.
questions.obtain: The owner states the intended scope. It changes the content plan more than any other open question, because breadth needs a competitor set this site does not have.

design_findings.title: The most important number on each page is a citation, and the way to buy is a footnote
design_findings.what_a_reader_sees: On a product page the eye is led to a source chip reading 'M4 · www.amazon.com Amazon listing'. There is no button and no statement of what happens if it is clicked; 71 of the 80 product links on the site are styled this way.
design_findings.why_it_matters: Affiliate revenue is a function of qualified clicks. A citation-labelled link is the weakest possible invitation to click, and it is the only invitation on the page.

design_findings.title: Twenty product pages, zero product images
design_findings.what_a_reader_sees: A dossier of tables and prose. Nothing to look at where the product should be.
design_findings.why_it_matters: Shoppers scan visually before they read. A page about an appliance that cannot show the appliance reads as second-hand, which is exactly the impression the complaint describes.

design_findings.title: The site's own methodology is the most repeated subject on the site
design_findings.what_a_reader_sees: Verification banners, source chips, blank-row explanations, an 'open items' strip and a methodology panel before any appliance is described in detail.
design_findings.why_it_matters: It is honest, and it is not what a reader came for. It also makes the prose read as a compliance artefact rather than as a publication, which is the definition of the impression the owner is complaining about.

design_findings.title: The primary call to action leads to a page with no product links
design_findings.what_a_reader_sees: A large button reading 'Which one to buy'.
design_findings.why_it_matters: Measured in PM-05: the destination, marketing/buying-guide.html, contains zero amazon.com/dp/ links, and it explicitly declines to name a winner. The site's most prominent promise is not kept by its destination.

design_findings.title: No page answers 'which one should I buy' with a shortlist
design_findings.what_a_reader_sees: Three individual write-ups, one comparison, and a guide that explains what it will not tell you.
design_findings.why_it_matters: The shortlist is the page type a shopper arrives from search expecting, and the page type Google's review guidance describes. Its absence removes both the ranking opportunity and the buying decision.

design_findings.title: The front door is a control room
design_findings.what_a_reader_sees: 76 navigation links in two groups, a KPI band, requirement counts, and a compliance ledger, before a shopper reaches a single product.
design_findings.why_it_matters: A first-time visitor decides in seconds whether the site is for them. A dashboard signals 'internal project' - and Amazon's licence requires the principal purpose to be marketing Amazon and driving sales.

design_findings.title: Every date printed on every page will be older than the freshness window
design_findings.why_it_matters: It is accurate today and self-defeating in eleven weeks. Amazon's review guidance asks for content generally within the last 60 days, so a printed date is a countdown that never resets itself.

design_findings.title: Nothing on the page tells a reader who wrote it or how
design_findings.what_a_reader_sees: No byline, no editor, no account of the pipeline that actually generated the page.
design_findings.why_it_matters: Search guidance asks who created the content and how, and calls fabricated authorship deception. The honest answer - generated from a sourced register - is unusual enough to be a genuine differentiator, and it is currently invisible.

design_findings.title: Several decision boards, and the choice is visible on none of them
design_findings.what_a_reader_sees: Suggestions, proposals and options - and no recorded selection anywhere.
design_findings.why_it_matters: The brief asks for a section where someone can choose the best path. Multiple sections each invite a choice and none records one, so a reviewer cannot tell which board is authoritative or which proposal was ever accepted.

ideas.title: Answer the freshness clock with one continuously updated page
ideas.trend_basis: Seasonal demand for air fryers peaks in November and December, and the site's pages are dated 2026-11-14/15 - the peak of that window.
ideas.article_concept: 'The air fryer question we get every November' - one page that is re-dated when it is genuinely re-read, carrying the three models' current official specs beside the same facts from the previous cycle so the reader sees what changed.
ideas.why_it_converts: It gives a returning reader a reason to come back and gives a search crawler a page whose visible date is current, which addresses the 60-day condition without inventing a fact.

ideas.title: The capacity arithmetic as an interactive tool, not an article
ideas.trend_basis: 'What size air fryer' is the buyer's first question, and the site already answers it in prose with the arithmetic worked out for exactly three models.
ideas.article_concept: A small, JS-free capacity calculator: enter the number of people and what you cook, get which of the three stated capacities the manufacturer's own page says fits that use. Every output links the sentence it came from.
ideas.why_it_converts: Google's guidance names 'functional page tools' as evidence of effort, and a tool is the one asset a competitor cannot copy by rewriting the prose.

ideas.title: A counter-footprint checker built from the published dimensions
ideas.trend_basis: The site already recorded that fit, not performance, is a common reason a countertop appliance is returned - and it publishes all three footprints in inches.
ideas.article_concept: 'Will it fit under my cabinet?' Enter your clear height and depth; the page compares them against the three published dimensions and says which fits, up to the limit of what a dimension can tell you.
ideas.why_it_converts: It converts a table row that is currently buried into the single reason a buyer abandons a purchase, and it is built entirely from facts already verified.

ideas.title: Two named-category heads rather than three competing brand pages
ideas.trend_basis: All three listings sit in the same Amazon category path. Two of the three are Chefman, so brand-level comparison is really model-level comparison.
ideas.article_concept: 'Chefman dual-basket vs Chefman single-basket: the two models that look alike and are not' and 'French-door oven or basket fryer: what the door changes' - each anchored to the published specs, not to brand adjectives.
ideas.why_it_converts: It targets the two queries a buyer types after deciding on a category, and it avoids the thin-affiliate trap of a page per brand with the same boilerplate.

ideas.title: A sourcing-contest page: invite a correction and publish the winner
ideas.trend_basis: The site's differentiator is that every number is sourced, and manufacturers publish conflicting numbers. That conflict is itself the most interesting content the site owns.
ideas.article_concept: 'Two official pages disagree about this air fryer. Here is both of them.' One page per disagreement, updated when either manufacturer's page changes, with the reader invited to send the page they found.
ideas.why_it_converts: It is original, it is checkable, it is impossible to generate without the sources, and it earns links from the only people who care - which is what organic traffic is built from.

irregularities.found: tools/build_decisions.py --check hashes every file under decisions/, generated or not
irregularities.effect: Any register stored in decisions/ is permanent drift against a fresh build. This session's own register hit it: validate_decisions failed until the file was moved.
irregularities.resolution: Moved to docs/review-board.json, the convention docs/discovery-t40.json already uses. No file owned by another session was edited.
irregularities.owner_action: None - closed by this session. Recorded because the trap is still live for the next session.

irregularities.found: The footer negation required by the Sec. 5 endorsement rule must sit on the same line as the phrase it negates
irregularities.effect: A first render split 'not' and 'affiliated with Amazon' across two lines and validate_data failed all four pages.
irregularities.resolution: Negation kept inside one element. The sentence was not weakened.
irregularities.owner_action: None - closed. Flagged because the rule is line-based, and the next author will hit it.

irregularities.found: Several decision boards publish proposals and none records a decision
irregularities.effect: A reviewer cannot tell which board is authoritative. The count is ambiguous: five boards carry proposals, six files exist counting decisions/index.html, which is a hub.
irregularities.resolution: Published with both readings rather than one (PM-09), and PS-12 proposes an index over consolidation.
irregularities.owner_action: Decide PS-12. Recorded here so the ambiguity is visible rather than tidied away.

irregularities.found: No browser render of the four new pages was possible in this environment
irregularities.effect: npx playwright install chromium fails with 'Download failure, code=1'. A screenshot test would have caught a layout defect that a structural check cannot.
irregularities.resolution: Checked instead: tags balance on all four pages (html.parser stack), the pages ship no script, and every internal href and fragment resolves. The gate now enforces the static/balance rule, so it will not regress silently.
irregularities.owner_action: Optional: open the four pages on a phone and report a layout problem if one appears.

irregularities.found: Six of the sixteen traced requirement rows rest on no official source
irregularities.effect: No official page defines what 'automates product research', a 'complete requirements list', or a review board must contain, so the judgement on those rows is this session's, not an authority's.
irregularities.resolution: Each such row says in its own words that no official page can settle it, and the gate fails a row that drops the source without that statement.
irregularities.owner_action: None. The distinction is published so that a sourced row and an unsourced one cannot be mistaken for each other.
